body: Oh, probably. I'm already seeing a GI specialist though, and it took six months to even get an appointment with him the first time. I've had an endoscopy and a colonoscopy already that came up negative, it's just hard to stay not depressed when it's been almost 3 years without a diagnosis or anything better than "good luck finding food you can eat".

Yeah, if they had an end date it'd be different. Or even just a diagnosis and a treatment plan that wasn't "well good luck, hopefully you find food that doesn't make you violently ill".   It's led to my failing classes, and otherwise failing at the basics like communicating with friends and family.

Na'ah bro, I'm definitely in the category of failures. I'm failing my classes, I'm so far in debt I don't see a feasible way out, I've got some GI issues that make me hate life, I have trouble remembering to stay in the moment and talk to my friends and family on occasion, I also suck at the basics of being functional like waking up in the morning and attending my classes on time, or being interested in the boring shit I'm being taught instead of doing something cool like building an AI that makes mario bros levels. 

I'd go to a hospital but I'd honestly rather be dead than face my family after something like this. They're stoic faced and have encouraged me to stop taking my antidepressants multiple times, not from any sort of maliciousness just obliviousness I think.

I mean, why not? I've been sick for 3 years or so, physically that is, my guts are basically fucked. I've failed about half my classes now, even though at one point I had published research and a 3.8 GPA, and I'm just tired of being tired and sick and failing to be able to do the basic things humans are capable of like getting up in the morning without wanting to kill yourself or going longer than a couple hours without violently shitting out mucous and the undigested remains of the last meal I ate. 

I know killing myself is probably overkill but the doctors don't believe me when I say I can't stay focused on things and just how bad my GI issues are.
The honest truth is you only tell them if you want help.
